v1_text: User can initiate and stop voice explicitly on Windows.
User can initiate and stop voice explicitly on Android.
Voice input produces visible finalized and optional partial transcript.
REVA responds with audible speech and visible text.
Session controller supports Listening, Processing, Speaking, Interrupted, Error and Idle.
User can interrupt TTS by voice or Stop button.
VAD/endpointing handles pauses without premature send in fixture suite.
Every session has cancel and timeout controls for STT, LLM and TTS.
Audio devices can be selected and device-loss handled.
Microphone mute and speaker mute are separately available.
Android foreground voice session has persistent, visible notification where required.
Android voice path checks on-device STT capability before selecting it.
Android TTS voice, rate and accessibility controls follow system availability.
Voice/typed turns share conversation history.
Session continuity after network disconnect is explicit.
Duplex and noise suppression are selectable as capabilities, not mandatory.
Multilingual STT/TTS support includes explicit active language and fallback.
Always-on wake word on Android only with reviewed platform-feasible mode.
Wake-word feature on Windows remains default-off and integrity-checked.
Voice recording history defaults to off, configurable only by consent.
Model-independent assistant interface supports deterministic test provider and opted-in real provider.
Dialog planner distinguishes answer vs tool proposal vs clarification.
Typed/tool payloads are validated against versioned schemas.
Windows actions use explicit allowlist, fixed targets and device context.
Close, delete, send, or other high-risk operations require explicit confirmation.
Every tool execution returns attempted/succeeded/failed/cancelled and evidence.
Policy engine denies by default on unknown capability/device or absent permission.
Phone actions use Android platform APIs/intents, not arbitrary shell.
Cross-device commands identify initiator, target and approval device.
Multi-step task plans run with bounded steps, budget and abort button.
Tools can be disabled individually in Settings.
Email/calendar integrations use least-scope delegated auth.
REVA can explain which action it executed, on which device, and when.
Third-party plugins run within scoped capability/approval boundary.
User can create and query explicit memories.
User can list, edit, archive, delete and export their saved memories.
Memory is not silently saved from every conversation.
Hybrid search combines lexical and semantic retrieval with safe fallback.
Conversation history can be cleared independently of memories.
Local Android data uses encrypted-at-rest protection for tokens/secrets.
Paired sync has per-device identity, revocation and permission scopes.
Pairing requires proximity/verification with an explicit one-time handshake.
Data sync is resumable, idempotent and conflict-aware.
Deletes take precedence over older updates.
User can choose which data classes sync.
Conversations and preferences are usable with both devices online or offline.
Complete export and deletion paths exist for supported local/synced data.
Optional encrypted relay supports off-LAN connections.
Life-memory entities Person/Event/Commitment can be opt-in.
Desktop has accessible voice controls, transcript and typed fallback.
APK has home, voice, text, memory, device, settings and permissions screens.
User can inspect provider/connection availability.
Pair/Unpair/Approve remote access can be completed in-app.
Settings disclose local/cloud processing for each active provider.
Conversation search and pinned sessions.
Local reminders and notifications support opt-in scheduling.
Windows installer includes runtime and supports uninstall/upgrade.
Android signed APK installs; Play distribution uses AAB.
Crash recovery shows unsent action status without duplicate execution.
User can wipe local state and revoke pairing.
All network endpoints bind loopback by default; no LAN listener unless pairing explicitly enabled.
Cross-device traffic uses TLS with authenticated device identity; reject unsigned/expired/revoked sessions.
Audio and model work must not block the WinUI UI thread; backpressure and bounded queues required.
Phone capture/recognition must not block Compose main thread; service lifecycle cleaned up.
Secrets never stored in plaintext config files or logged; migrate local Core token to OS secret storage before R4.
Local mobile security uses OWASP MASVS controls for storage, authentication, crypto, network, platform, privacy.
Cancelled sessions do not execute pending tools or play stale TTS.
Test runs never point to a user's real REVA_DATA_DIR; fixtures are isolated.
Errors are typed and actionable; preserve correlation IDs across clients and Core without recording microphone bytes.
p50, p95, memory, CPU, battery and thermal behavior profiled on documented devices.
Dependencies pinned, SBOM published, release artifacts signed and checksummed.
No permanent permission requirement for phone microphone; revoke during session handled.
Model and tool prompts treated as untrusted; retrieved memory/webpage text never grants permissions.
Access checks enforce user × device × capability × session × action risk on server and target.
Local-first feature behavior documented by connectivity state (offline, LAN, internet).
A user can turn off telemetry and erase user event traces; security-only local logs have documented retention.
Preserve existing `reva_core` FastAPI routes and WinUI behavior while adding versioned capabilities.
Keep a single process modular Core and internal dependency boundaries.
Central `SessionCoordinator` owns exactly one active voice turn per session.
Session IDs, turn IDs and correlation IDs propagate through STT/LLM/TTS/tool events.
Typed event schema includes `schema_version`, `event_id`, `sequence`, `timestamp`, `device_id`, `session_id`, `turn_id`, `kind` and `payload`.
Protocol evolution is additive within a major version; unknown required major is rejected.
Cancellation token/epoch invalidates all older pending provider responses.
Provider deadlines exist separately for VAD/STT, model, tool and TTS.
No client takes a database file handle outside its owning device process.
Windows Core API remains loopback and bearer-auth protected; remote access only through paired gateway.
Android contracts generated/shared from versioned JSON Schema/OpenAPI; no handwritten divergent event types.
Configuration resolution is explicit per user/device/provider with encrypted secrets.
Graceful upgrade migrates schemas without losing data; rollback compatibility declared.
Audio capture and TTS playback are pluggable native adapters.
Bounded audio input/output buffers prevent OOM; drop strategy never silently executes partial commands.
Voice session has one active audio producer per selected microphone, arbitrated with wake word.
TTS output carries the originating `turn_epoch`; on interrupt obsolete frames are discarded.
Partial transcript must not trigger sensitive actions; only stabilized final user intent enters policy.
Provider-specific STT/TTS types remain behind protocol interfaces; selection driven by capability.
Stale provider response cannot rewrite current composer, history or spoken output.
Low-confidence tool phrase results in clarification, not speculative execution.
Pre-recorded clips are used for deterministic transcript/turn regression; physical-mic suite opt-in.
Microphone activation indicator derived from actual resource state, not only UI requested state.
Android checks on-device STT availability and discloses use of fallback recognizer.
Android stops mic promptly when activity/foreground-service lifecycle disallows access.
Network media events are authenticated and have ordered stream recovery or clean session restart.
Turn-end and barge-in thresholds configurable and measured by device/provider.
Record per-turn timings: user speech end, STT final, LLM first token, TTS first byte, playback first sample.
Background/noise test corpora include silence, overlap, echo, accents, short commands, long utterances.
Model can request only registered capabilities; tool calls are not raw shell commands.
Action proposal is schema-validated and normalized before policy check.
Risk tier calculated independently of model-provided hints.
Approval binds action ID, canonical arguments, target ID, scope and TTL.
Executor records success with actual OS/provider evidence, failure and unknown outcomes.
Unsafe action is denied when confirmation absent, stale, ambiguous or sourced only from speech for sensitive tier.
Paired phone never obtains PC OS process handles or a generic remote-execute API.
Remote operations are authorized against sender identity AND target policy.
Android actions use sanctioned platform APIs and respect runtime grants.
Multi-step plans carry max steps, max runtime, total tool budget and cancel propagation.
Action ledger has immutable outcome record and redacted arguments with user-facing inspection.
Pairing key agreement authenticated by explicit user-approved QR/fingerprint.
Gateway TLS and device auth required for any paired connection.
Paired keys scoped to only approved actions/data classes.
Pairing grants revocable with atomic check before dispatch.
Gateway binds to LAN only when user enables remote access and reports interface/port.
No remote caller can invoke Core unrestricted `/v1/*` API.
Stream reconnect requires authenticated resume token and deduplicates prior events.
Credentials rotate and support device-key compromise recovery.
Security logs record which device made each data/tool request, without raw secrets.
Core memory repository supports explicit create/query/update/archive/delete/export.
Deletion removes retrieval eligibility, removes/invalidate embeddings and records redacted audit.
Hybrid retrieval falls back to lexical on embedding/Ollama failures.
Local user files and voice temporary buffers have bounded lifecycle.
Android caches only scoped, needed records; keys live in Keystore.
Schema migrations are transactional, versioned and testable with copied DB.
Sync applies per-record idempotent events and durable outbox acknowledgment.
Conflict policy avoids wall-clock-only last-write-wins for deletes.
Data-scope settings apply to sync send and receive sides.
Export includes human-readable memory/conversation data and documented omissions.
Wipe and unpair revoke credentials and clear queue/embeddings/local caches.
Android minSdk and targetSdk determined by device support + current Play requirements, recorded in build.
Runtime microphone permission requested only on explicit user gesture.
Foreground service type/notification and background-start restrictions honored by API level.
Use on-device recognizer only when availability check passes; otherwise disclose fallback.
Recognizer and TTS lifecycle destroyed/shut down on completion.
No `QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES`, Accessibility automation or privileged settings as a shortcut.
Local app functions survive permanent denial of microphone permission.
Phone can select independent model provider instead of paired PC.
Standalone AI mode communicates data-processing route and network requirements.
Signed release APK/AAB validated for installation, upgrade and rollback behavior.
UI/main threads remain responsive under slow STT/LLM/TTS.
Python Core process lifecycle distinguishes owned vs external.
No raw microphone byte payloads in normal logs.
Connection and model capability changes cause explicit UI statuses.
Every queue has documented upper bound and handling on saturation.
End-to-end voice trace latency budgets recorded per device/provider.
Battery and heat budget measured for active and background-allowed voice mode.
Windows packaging includes Core interpreter/runtime and model-install guidance.
Release build signs artifacts and generates SBOM/checksums.
Security signoff covers Android MASVS, transport, policy, secrets and privacy.
Reliability tests exercise disconnect, service kill, permission loss, device sleep and stale actions.
Structured telemetry is opt-in, scoped and redacted, and can be removed by user.
User can ask a free-form question and receive a response from a selected, disclosed real model; fake model clearly marked developer-only.
Tool-calling LLM returns strictly validated `answer`, `clarify`, `propose_action`, or `propose_plan`; malformed output is refused, not executed.
REVA recognizes direct, allowlisted open/close requests without a slow LLM call when rules are unambiguous.
User can use a voice command to launch Chrome, Notepad, VS Code or another explicitly configured supported app; app-open result must be observed.
User sees and can stop AI thinking, STT, tool and TTS states; cancelled turns cannot resume previous tools or audio.
User can ask what REVA can currently control; response derives from live device capabilities, not model guesses.
Voice assistant only speaks “done” if native executor returned verified success, otherwise reports the limitation.
Sensitive actions require explicit, targeted confirmation and cannot be approved solely by model-generated text or untrusted UI content.
User can select local vs provider reasoning and see whether audio/screens/text leave device.
Per-turn source-provenance and redacted activity history disclose tool proposals, approvals, observed outcomes and timeouts.
Windows user can explicitly invoke “inspect this window” and see the accessible UI tree with sensitive fields redacted and scope indicator.
Windows user can say “click [named visible control]” in a supported app; REVA grounds to a current UIA element, rejects ambiguity and checks postcondition.
REVA prefers an app-specific supported API/intent over UI clicks where available; unsupported app does not trigger blind coordinate clicks.
Untrusted screen/document text is treated as data, not system instructions; injected UI content cannot change authorization or granted tools.
Android APK supports voice, answers, app launch via intents, and clearly scoped local device actions; denial is recoverable.
Pairing a phone to PC presents device identity, action scope, confirmation target and revocation; phone never obtains PC unrestricted shell access.
Windows and Android report their distinct tool support; phone never claims to support PC-only controls or vice versa.
Screen screenshots are captured only within an active, consented task and erased when no longer necessary; sensitive contents excluded where APIs allow.
An explicitly activated bounded Windows workflow supports at least three dependent steps with independent verification and a cancel button.
“Find a file and attach it to a draft” remains a **draft** until a separate send approval; approval binds exact recipient, attachment and destination.
A failed or ambiguous UI action halts the plan or asks for help, never blindly repeats potentially non-idempotent actions.
VLM can locate unlabeled Windows UI targets using on-demand screenshots after semantic UIA lookup fails; it never silently authorizes clicks.
Android Play distribution does not rely on autonomous AI planning+execution through AccessibilityService unless legitimately eligible under the current verified exception.
Android on-device or hosted reasoning continues to answer basic questions even when paired Windows PC is offline.
Agent capabilities, language/vision models and providers are empirically benchmarked by hardware class, privacy mode and task success.
REVA explains which screen element it used and why it stopped when a task cannot be grounded.
Advanced Android UI control via AccessibilityService is available only after product-purpose, legal/store-policy and user-consent review; never assumed universal.
Hands-free always-listening Android wake word is offered only when technically and policy permitted for the device/session state.
`ModelProvider` interface supports `complete`, optional streaming, typed tool responses, timeout, cancel, model identity.
`Planner` consumes user turn, sanitized context, retrieved memory, live capability registry; not raw OS authority.
Only schema-approved action kinds enter `ActionPolicy`; free-form shell, executable path and arbitrary URL/script are rejected.
Policy derives action risk from registered capability + normalized args, not LLM-proposed tier.
Approval is cryptographically or equivalent securely bound to operation, canonical args, user, device, expiry and request ID.
Session coordinator owns cancel epoch and ignores late STT, model and tool results.
`ExecutionResult` separates attempted, observed, verified, failed, denied, unknown; fabricated success prohibited.
Direct known commands may be deterministic to reduce model latency and hallucinations.
A single bounded LLM planning loop suffices initially; no swarm/agent-to-agent privilege delegation.
Model selection depends on measured tool-call accuracy, latency, footprint, privacy and hardware; no unbenchmarked “best model” label.
Critical observations are never promoted from an unverified model narration; executor supplies evidence.
Screen and tool output strings are marked untrusted, delimited, redacted and excluded from policy instructions.
Streaming voice events carry turn ID, sequence, cancellation ID and trace timings.
Audio path can fall back from streamed chunks to buffered transcription/TTS with declared UX change.
Existing real-STT and TTS opt-in tests remain gated and must not be reported as hardware proof when skipped.
Windows native executor owns process launch, UIA tree, InvokePattern/ValuePattern and postcondition verification.
UI target reference includes short-lived snapshot ID, target app/window identity, element identifier and timestamp.
UIA and safe OS integration are preferred; coordinate injection only after fresh grounding and explicit interactive session.
Input events are never sent to the wrong foreground window; elevated/secure desktops fail closed.
Password fields, OTPs, private notifications and secure screens are masked or excluded from model observations when feasible; never intentionally bypass OS safeguards.
VLM screenshot request is an independent consented, bounded capture; no passive screen recording or raw screenshot logging.
Android `Intent`/public app APIs and content URIs take precedence over AccessibilityService.
Android UI and screen APIs require appropriate foreground lifecycle, runtime permissions and disclosure.
Accessibility use is feature-gated to store-policy-reviewed narrow, user-directed workflows; do not ship unrestricted agentic control.
MediaProjection is opt-in per session and follows foreground-service/system-consent requirements.
Remote pairing gateway checks peer identity, scope, replay, TTL and per-device revocation before any PC operation.
Native adapter transport is an implementation detail; model decisions share typed semantics over existing HTTP/WebSocket or later verified gRPC.
Adapter execution grants are issued by trusted policy component; executors validate binding to action, target, expiry, actor and idempotency key.
Task engine supports DAG/ordered steps, step cap, wall-clock cap, memory/tool token budget, cancel and human checkpoints.
Each state-changing step has a declared precondition and postcondition; non-idempotent steps never auto-replay after unknown outcome.
VLM is a **grounding fallback** and returns candidate elements with uncertainty; separate policy+native execution still governs actuation.
RAG only retrieves explicit retained user memory and consented resources; deletion removes embedding/FTS exposure.
Android standalone model or hosted provider is separately configured with consent, minimum device capacity and explicit fallback.
Benchmarks report task-completion, tool call schema validity, action false-success, ASR WER, first audible response and barge-in.
Evaluation splits synthetic/consented fixtures from live physical runs; model/provider versions pinned in evidence.
Prompt templates, model config, capability registry, policy tables and data retention are versioned as artifacts.
